MOA stands for "minute of angle". Picture a circle of 360 degrees, and your gun is pointed straight at 0 degrees (really it's a sphere since you aim up/down and side to side). Each degree can be divided into 60 "minutes". If you fire straight at 0 degrees, 0 minutes, your gun should theoretically hit right at 0 degrees, 0 minutes... but it probably won't because the bullet never flies precisely straight consistently every time. There's wind, imperfections in the bullet or the barrel, etc. So "1 MOA" means that your gun hits consistently within 1 minute (proportion of 1 degree)-- aiming at zero you'd be landing consistently withing 1 minute of zero. The farther away the target is, the more that 1 MOA represents in terms of distance on the target. It just so happens that 1 MOA at 100 yards is about 1 inch (1.047"). So 1 MOA at 25 yards is about 1/4 inch, 1 MOA at 50 yards is about 1/2 inch, 1 MOA at 200 yards is about 2", etc.

I think usually when people say a gun is 1 MOA or say they shoot 1 MOA they mean that they're that accurate at a certain distance like 100 yards, or maybe 300 yards or more for long distance shooters. Obviously the bullet will move off the target more the longer you're shooting due to wind etc. so even a 1 MOA gun may not always hit at 2" at 200 yards even though it might get within 1/2 inch at 50 yards consistently.
